gaps.sentence: This year the festival attracted ___ visitors than in 2024.
gaps.explanation: 'Fewer' is the comparative for countable plurals like visitors; 'less' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: ___ the food was eaten within minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'All the food' is correct with an uncountable noun; 'whole' needs 'the whole of' and 'both' needs two separate items.

gaps.hint: an unspecified day in the future
gaps.explanation: 'Another day' means some other, unspecified day; 'the other day' refers to the recent past.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my two brothers work in banking.
gaps.explanation: 'Both of my two brothers work ...' is correct; 'all' and 'none' are not used for two.
'Several charges' means more than two; the other options are used only with uncountable nouns.

gaps.sentence: The hotel was full, so we had to look for ___ hotel.
gaps.explanation: 'Another hotel' means some other, unspecified one; 'the other hotel' would imply exactly two known hotels.

gaps.sentence: It cost a great ___ of money to repair the roof.
gaps.explanation: 'A great deal of' is used with uncountable nouns like money; 'a great lot of' and 'a great plenty of' do not exist.
'Neither of my parents is ...' is correct for two items with a singular verb; 'both/all' need a plural verb and 'none' is not used for two.
